- We'll temporarily rebalance kv_priority_shards for your pool to round-robin allocation (should reduce HOL blocking).

Quick triage notes / root cause hypothesis:

I pulled the lane dumps and traces from the dd-export. Summary: lane 3 (BrightBridge production pool) is exhibiting very large batch formation — median batch size jumped from ~48 tokens to ~1024 tokens during the initial spike window. The batching heuristic "batch_glide_window_ms" was set to 1500ms in the tenant override (non-default); combined with kv_priority_shards uneven mapping, requests targeting the hot keysets are queued behind long-running batches. This is classic HOL gating at the lane boundary, which both increases p99 and surfaces backend 500s when internal timeouts for prefetches trigger.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (can be applied live without model restarts):
1) Set batch_glide_window_ms -> 0 (disable glide) for tenant: redwoodctl tenant override set-brightbridge batch_glide_window_ms=0
2) Force max_batch_tokens=1024 -> 256 for the active model variant: redwoodctl runtime update --tenant brightbridge --max_batch_tokens 256
3) Rebalance KV priority to round-robin across shards: redwoodctl kv rebalance --tenant brightbridge --mode round_robin
4) Short-term eviction policy tweak: kv_eviction=LRU-ttl-5m to avoid thrash during the next 10m

I attached the KB playbook with the exact commands (playbook_kv_tuning_v2.pdf). I’ll run 1+2 now, will follow up once done.

- Markus Klein
Principal, Serving Runtime

I executed Markus' mitigations at 08:33 UTC: disabled glide, reduced max_batch_tokens, and kicked a quick rebalance of KV shards. Summary of immediate impact:
- Error rate (500s) dropped from ~9.8% to 0.9% over two rolling minutes.
- P99 dropped from ~1.8s to ~280ms within 4 minutes.
- Throughput is stable; slight increase in CPU due to smaller batches but within margin.

Customer comms suggestion: offer a 24-hour service credit and a short maintenance window tomorrow night to roll in a config patch that prevents tenant-overrides from increasing batch_glide_window_ms past 500ms.

Note for leadership: this was not a model regression or infra hardware failure; it was a config interaction (batching heuristic + KV priority skew). Going forward we should:
- Harden tenant override validation for batching heuristics
- Add an automated detector for large-batch formation on a single lane that fires early and throttles glide heuristics

I’ll attach the dd trace bundle and the lane dump.

— Rishi Malhotra
SRE, Serving Runtime

Subject: Exec brief: BrightBridge outage window — batching/KV config caused transient HOL blocking (closed)

Executive summary (one line):
- BrightBridge saw elevated p99 and 500s between 08:00–08:36 UTC due to tenant override that allowed an aggressive batching "glide" heuristic combined with skewed KV priority shards; engineering applied mitigations and error rates returned to baseline.

Key facts:
- Impact window: 08:00–08:36 UTC on 2028-07-10.
- Actions taken: disabled batch_glide heuristic, reduced max_batch_tokens for the model variant, rebalanced KV priority shards, tweaked eviction policy. All changes applied live; no model restarts.
- Customer impact: transient user-facing 500s (~9% peak) and increased p99 to ~1.8s. Services recovered; no data loss.
- Customer remediation: offered 24-hour service credit and proposed an overnight maintenance window to harden tenant config.

Root cause: permissive tenant override + batch_glide_window_ms set to 1500ms combined with uneven kv_priority_shards mapping. The interaction allowed large queued batches that blocked hot-key lanes (HOL).

Proposed follow-ups (owners / ETA):
- Engineering (Markus) — add validation to tenant override service to cap batch_glide_window_ms <= 500ms (ETA: 2 days)
- Runtime (Rishi) — implement a detector to throttle glide when lane-specific batch sizes exceed expected thresholds (ETA: 1 week)
- CS/Ops (Sofia) — complete customer communications and credit (ETA: immediate / 24h credit issued)
- PM (Marissa) — require postmortem and include in the next reliability roadmap discussion (JIRA-OPS-4821)

Attachments: playbook_kv_tuning_v2.pdf (internal playbook), dd-trace-logs.zip, kv-lane-dump-20280710.tar.gz
